_comment: Ground truth for Exp 3a probe targets P1-P4 (exp3a §Probe Targets). Hand-written per PLAN.md §9 decision 5 so each property has a known label rather than a post-hoc annotation. Paths are relative to repo/.
_test_note: Tests are unittest.TestCase subclasses, so both runners collect them and the sandbox needs no third-party packages installed.

baseline._failure_note: All three trace to one missing function, so a partial fix is distinguishable from a complete one: adding throughput_mib_s alone clears 2 of 3 and leaves the report test red.

p1_file_graph._depth_note: report -> stats -> units is a 3-level chain, so the fix cannot be made from one file in isolation: the unit basis is decided in units.py, applied in stats.py, and surfaced in report.py.

p4_ambiguity.question: Which mebi-scale unit basis should throughput use?
p4_ambiguity._design_note: P4 needs variance, not a constant label. srcpkg/units.py offers both conversions and srcpkg/stats.py's docstring never says which a throughput figure takes, so an agent is genuinely in 'multiple_candidates' until it reads tests/test_stats.py, and 'committed' after. An agent that guesses mebibits produces 8.0 and fails, making the commitment externally checkable from the test result rather than only from a self-report.

delegation_relevance._note: Why this fixture tests the channel rather than just the model, under Binding A (orchestrator = Summarizer 2B, worker = Code expert 3B) with Latent-DA stubbing the ToolMessage (PLAN.md §6).
delegation_relevance.worker_must_discover: the unit basis, which is pinned only in tests/test_stats.py
delegation_relevance.orchestrator_must_learn: which basis the worker committed to, in order to accept or correct the report wiring
delegation_relevance.failure_signature_if_channel_carries_not: report.summarize is wired with the wrong basis or the throughput line is omitted, so tests/test_report.py stays red while tests/test_stats.py may pass
